questions.prompt: A laptop requests a file from a host, then shares its own printer with another laptop. Which conclusion about client and server roles is correct?

choices.text: A laptop can never provide a server function
choices.explanation: Device form factor does not prohibit serving requests.

choices.text: A server must always initiate every request
choices.explanation: Clients generally initiate the service requests in these examples.

choices.text: One device can act as a client in one exchange and a server in another
choices.explanation: Roles depend on which service interaction is being considered.

choices.text: Using Ethernet makes both devices routers
choices.explanation: Ethernet attachment does not confer routing functionality.

questions.explanation: Client and server describe service roles. A machine can consume one service while providing another.

choices.explanation: Wireless names do not determine optical compatibility.

choices.text: Whether the modules support the installed fiber type and distance
choices.explanation: Module reach is specified for particular fiber characteristics.

choices.explanation: Descriptions are administrative text, not signaling requirements.

choices.explanation: Transport receipt does not establish application persistence.

questions.prompt: An IPv6 anycast instance keeps advertising its service route after the application process fails. Network routing remains healthy. Which conclusion is sound?

choices.text: Anycast automatically verifies that every application transaction succeeds
choices.explanation: Ordinary routing does not inherently validate the application service.

choices.text: A shared anycast address guarantees traffic can never reach a failed process
choices.explanation: The unhealthy instance can remain selected while its route is advertised.

choices.text: Routing may continue directing traffic to that unhealthy instance until reachability is adjusted
choices.explanation: Service health must be connected to route advertisement or another explicit recovery mechanism.

choices.text: IPv6 multicast immediately delivers copies to every other service instance
choices.explanation: Anycast forwarding does not become multicast replication on application failure.

questions.explanation: An available network route is not proof of a functioning service. An anycast design needs explicit health handling if application failure should remove an instance from selection.

choices.text: A new SSID for the Ethernet interface
choices.explanation: The interface already reaches its local Ethernet LAN.

choices.text: A larger TCP receive window
choices.explanation: A transport window cannot create a missing route.

choices.explanation: Downlink reception alone cannot prove the uplink.

choices.explanation: SSID names do not determine received RF power.

choices.text: The client must transmit at the AP’s configured wattage
choices.explanation: Client power is separately constrained and configured.

choices.text: Coverage must support both AP-to-client and client-to-AP communication
choices.explanation: A one-sided power increase can leave an asymmetric link budget.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements apply when an ordinary Layer 2 switch forwards a known unicast frame within one VLAN? Select two.

choices.text: It uses the destination MAC lookup to select the output port
choices.explanation: The learned destination mapping guides forwarding.

choices.text: It decrements the packet’s IP TTL
choices.explanation: Ordinary Layer 2 switching is not an IP routing hop.

choices.text: It changes the destination IP to the switch address
choices.explanation: Transparent bridging does not perform that rewrite.

choices.text: It always floods every forwarding port
choices.explanation: A known destination normally permits directed forwarding.

choices.text: It can learn or refresh the source MAC entry on ingress
choices.explanation: Source learning and destination forwarding are separate operations.

questions.explanation: A known destination avoids unknown-unicast flooding. Learning the source can still occur during the same received frame.

questions.prompt: A voice deployment uses VLAN 150 for phones and VLAN 50 for attached PCs. The access switch performs only Layer 2 switching, and the VLAN 150 gateway is beyond its uplinks. choices.explanation: Separating voice at the edge is insufficient unless that VLAN reaches its Layer 3 attachment.

choices.text: Increase the access port’s STP priority.
choices.explanation: STP port priority does not add VLANs to an allowed list.

choices.explanation: The deployment explicitly places voice in tagged VLAN 150.

choices.text: Move the PC into VLAN 150.
choices.explanation: This does not repair the missing voice path and changes the intended separation.

Configuration summary:
Vlan60 address: 10.60.0.254/24
Administrative state: enabled
Line protocol: down
SVI autostate: default (no override)

choices.text: There is no operational Layer 2 forwarding member for VLAN 60.
choices.explanation: Default SVI autostate depends on an active forwarding attachment in its VLAN.

choices.text: An SVI requires two active access ports.
choices.explanation: One eligible forwarding member is sufficient under ordinary autostate behavior.

choices.text: The SVI’s IP address must end in .1.
choices.explanation: Any suitable unicast host address in the subnet can be a gateway.

choices.text: VLAN 60 is outside the normal VLAN range.
choices.explanation: VLAN 60 is a normal-range VLAN.
